A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BridgeDrive study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v2 reports original Bench2Drive simulations, waypoint and anchor ablations, qualitative failure cases, and NAVSIM results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds outcomes for a LEAD-trained BridgeDrive variant in Appendix E, Tables 10–11.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the specified anchor construction from clustering trajectories then averaging speeds to jointly clustering geometry and speed. Appendix C.3 specifies L1 instead of the previously stated MSE loss. New Appendix E adapts BridgeDrive to geometry-only anchors and outputs, with LEAD perception and speed control. These are limited procedural revisions within the retained diffusion-bridge framework; they do not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds training with LEAD's expert-generated CARLA dataset, extending training-data coverage within the existing driving domain. The PDM-Lite experiments and NAVSIM navtest evaluation are retained; NAVSIM's relocation does not add coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 10 introduces TFv6 from Nguyen et al. (2026) as a comparator for the LEAD-trained variant. Comparator membership in the matched Bench2Drive, NAVSIM and ablation tables is otherwise unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix C.3 replaces the statement that BridgeDrive uses 20 anchors with a statement identifying 60 as optimal, consistent with the already-existing Table 9 sweep. Appendix E adds a configuration using frozen LEAD perception and 10-epoch denoiser/classifier training. The PDFs do not establish reruns of the retained experiments.

E4.justification: The waypoint-representation, anchor-ranking, anchor-only/regression and anchor-count ablations are retained, as are the qualitative examples and Appendix B.3 failure case. The LEAD addition reports another training configuration's benchmark results, without a distinct controlled ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: Both versions state three random seeds for models exceeding the previous SOTA and already report uncertainty with ± values. The added LEAD rows extend that reporting style; no changed run-count policy, uncertainty estimator or significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Matched earlier numerical results are retained. Tables 10–11 add LEAD-variant results: DS 95.42, SR 86.06% and mean multi-ability score 81.28%; TFv6 scores DS 95.2 and SR 86.8%. These are additional results under changed training/model conditions. Appendix E's stated 0.72-point SR deficit disagrees with the table-derived 0.74 points.

T1.justification: The diffusion and bridge equations, score approximation and mathematical training formulation remain unchanged, with no new proof or substantive derivation. The L1 implementation statement is not accompanied by a revision explaining its relationship to the retained MSE-based formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same anchor-guided diffusion-bridge contribution, forward/reverse consistency rationale, real-time ODE-sampling claim and 7.72-percentage-point Bench2Drive advantage. The LEAD experiment does not redefine the headline contributions.

C2.justification: v3 removes the explicit lidar-dependence limitation, drops the assertion that NAVSIM performance is saturated, and moderates criticism of its evaluation setting. Appendix E adds an interpretation of generalization across training datasets. The multi-ability caption now acknowledges Overtake as well as Give Way as exceptions to superiority, matching the retained scores.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project/repository pointer and documents the LEAD variant's frozen perception module, 60 geometry-only anchors, 10-epoch training and delegated speed control. It also revises the clustering, loss and anchor-count specifications. The PDFs establish the new access pointer, not the repository's actual contents or availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds Nguyen et al. (2026) and discusses LEAD's treatment of learner–expert asymmetry to motivate Appendix E. The existing related-work discussion and positioning relative to DiffusionDrive and diffusion-bridge research are retained.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, Bench2Drive setup and main results are consolidated, and the revised NAVSIM discussion moves from Appendix B.4 to Section 4.3. Appendix E and publication/correspondence information are added. Most explanatory prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 10–11, moves NAVSIM's Table 6 to main-text Table 3, regroups comparator rows and adjusts table highlighting and placement. Figure images are retained; Figure 3's caption corrects four frames to three. These are limited display and layout revisions.

improvement.justification: The clearest gains are improved reproducibility through resolving the 20-versus-60-anchor inconsistency, documenting the LEAD adaptation, and correcting the overtaking caption. The more measured NAVSIM discussion also improves accuracy. Benefits are limited by the unreconciled L1/MSE distinction, removal of the lidar caveat, and retained headline SOTA language despite TFv6's higher success rate in the new comparison. The LEAD scores therefore do not establish an unqualified performance improvement.
